title: What If Your Body Never Got Vitamin C? Sailors Found Out

scenes.text: What if your body never got vitamin C? For sailors, the answer killed more than two million.
Humans can't skip it. Without vitamin C, gums swell and bleed, and old wounds can reopen.
On one voyage in the 1740s, about 1,400 of 1,900 crew died of scurvy or starvation.
In 1747, surgeon James Lind tested six remedies on 12 sick sailors. Oranges and lemons largely cured them.
Even then the Royal Navy waited decades. It only began issuing lemon juice in 1795.
The cure was a squeeze of citrus, and it took almost fifty years to act on it.
